info.title: FHIR Validator HTTP Service
info.description:
HTTP API exposed by the HL7 FHIR Validator when it is run in server mode:

    java -jar validator_cli.jar server <port> [options]

The service is a thin HTTP wrapper (`com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer`) around a single
in-process `ValidationEngine`. The engine is configured once at start up (FHIR version,
terminology server, loaded IGs, default instance-validator settings) and is then shared by
every request; per-request query parameters override the instance-validator settings for
that request only.

Notes that apply to the whole API:

* There is no authentication, no authorization and no rate limiting. By default the server
  binds to the loopback address only; `-allowNetworkAccess` binds to all interfaces and is
  the caller's responsibility to secure.
* The server is created with the default executor, so requests are handled one at a time on
  the dispatcher thread. The engine is stateful and mutable (`/loadIG` changes it for every
  subsequent request), so it is not safe to treat this as a shared multi-tenant service.
* Request format is taken from `Content-Type`: a media type containing `xml` means XML and
  one containing `json` means JSON. A body that declares neither - including one sent with no
  `Content-Type` - is refused with `415`, so a browser cannot drive the server from another
  page with a CORS-simple request. An empty body is not subject to this check.
* Response format is taken from `Accept`: a media type containing `xml` means XML, anything
  else means JSON. `/convert` and `/transform` use this to pick their *output* format;
  `/snapshot`, `/narrative`, `/version` and `/testdata` echo the *input* (or requested)
  format instead.
* Errors are returned as a FHIR `OperationOutcome` (`application/fhir+json` or
  `application/fhir+xml`), except for a wrong HTTP method, which returns `text/plain`.
* Paths are registered as `HttpServer` contexts, so any longer path with the same prefix
  also matches (e.g. `POST /validateResource/anything` is handled by `/validateResource`).

post.description:
Validates the posted resource against the base specification for the FHIR version the
server was started with, plus any profiles supplied in `Resource.meta.profile` or in the
`profile` query parameter.

Every query parameter is optional, but an **unrecognised** parameter name is an error:
the request fails with `400` and an `OperationOutcome` reading
`Unable to process param <name>=<value>`. The same `400` is returned when a value cannot
be parsed (`bestPractice`, `checkDisplay`, `resourceIdRule`, and the three numeric
parameters).

Enum values are case sensitive where the underlying enum is matched by name
(`bestPractice`, `checkDisplay`) and case insensitive where it is matched by code
(`resourceIdRule`, `level`, `questionnaire`, `htmlInMarkdown`,
`r5BundleRelativeReferencePolicy`).

parameters.name: profile
parameters.description: Canonical URL of a profile to validate against, as if it were listed in `Resource.meta.profile`. Repeat the parameter for multiple profiles. The profile and its dependencies must already be loaded (server start up `-ig`, or `/loadIG`).

parameters.name: extension
parameters.description: URL domain from which extensions are allowed, or `any` for all. Repeat for multiple domains.

parameters.name: bundleValidationRule
parameters.description: Selects entries within a Bundle to validate against a profile: a resource name, an integer index, or both. Must be paired positionally with `bundleValidationProfile` - the *n*th rule is matched with the *n*th profile, and unmatched extras are ignored.

parameters.name: bundleValidationProfile
parameters.description: Canonical URL of the profile applied to the matching `bundleValidationRule`.

parameters.name: jurisdiction
parameters.description: Jurisdiction to validate in. Use `uv` or `global` for no specific jurisdiction.

parameters.name: expansionParameters
parameters.description: Reference to expansion parameters to use - supplies fixed versions for code systems and value sets.

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: Minimum severity of message to report.

parameters.name: bestPractice
parameters.description: How best practice constraints are reported. Case sensitive - the value must match the enum constant exactly.

parameters.name: checkDisplay
parameters.description: How the display text on `Coding`/`CodeableConcept` is checked. Case sensitive - the value must match the enum constant exactly.

parameters.name: resourceIdRule
parameters.description: Whether the outermost resource must carry `Resource.id`. Contained resources (always required) and Bundle entries (always optional) are unaffected.

parameters.name: questionnaire
parameters.description: What to do when validating `QuestionnaireResponse`: `none` ignores the questionnaire reference, `check` validates against it when present, `required` demands one.

parameters.name: htmlInMarkdown
parameters.description: Issue level reported for embedded HTML found in markdown elements.

parameters.name: r5BundleRelativeReferencePolicy
parameters.description: Whether relative references in a Bundle follow the R5 resolution rule. An unrecognised value raises an unhandled exception rather than a `400`.

parameters.name: assumeValidRestReferences
parameters.description: Assume references that look like RESTful URLs are valid, and infer the resource type from the URL.

parameters.name: hintAboutNonMustSupport
parameters.description: Raise a hint for data elements not marked `mustSupport`.

parameters.name: wantInvariantsInMessages
parameters.description: Include the FHIRPath of a failed invariant in the message.

parameters.name: noInvariants
parameters.description: Do not check invariants at all.

parameters.name: unknownCodeSystemsCauseErrors
parameters.description: Treat an unknown code system behind a required binding as an error instead of a warning.

parameters.name: forPublication
parameters.description: Also check conformance with the `Shareable*` profiles.

parameters.name: noUnicodeBidiControlChars
parameters.description: Report any Unicode BiDi control character as an error.

parameters.name: verbose
parameters.description: Shorthand: sets crumb trails (hints explaining which profiles were applied) and `showMessageIds` together.

parameters.name: showMessageIds
parameters.description: Include message ids in the validation messages.

parameters.name: allowExampleUrls
parameters.description: Treat references to `example.org` URLs as valid.

parameters.name: showReferenceMessages
parameters.description: Include the detailed messages produced while validating referenced resources against the profiles declared on the reference.

parameters.name: securityChecks
parameters.description: Check that string content contains no HTML-like tags.

parameters.name: noExperimentalContent
parameters.description: Reject experimental content.

parameters.name: txRouting
parameters.description: Add output summarising which terminology server was used for each terminology operation.

parameters.name: implicitFhirpathStringConversions
parameters.description: Restore pre-5.6.48 FHIRPath automatic string conversion behaviour.

parameters.name: allowDoubleQuotesInFhirpath
parameters.description: Accept legacy FHIRPath statements that use double quotes.

parameters.name: maxValidationMessages
parameters.description: Stop validating once this many messages have been produced, and return what has been found so far. Values of `0` or less are ignored.

parameters.name: validationTimeout
parameters.description: Stop validating after this many milliseconds and return what has been found so far.

parameters.name: codeSystemValidationSizeLimit
parameters.description: Maximum number of codes checked against a code system for a single ValueSet include, ConceptMap group or CodeSystem supplement. Where a resource carries more codes than this, none are checked and a hint is issued instead. `0` means no limit.

parameters.name: htmlOutput
parameters.description: Accepted for parity with the CLI, but has no effect in server mode - the HTML summary is only written by the command line `validate` command.

parameters.name: outputStyle
parameters.description: Accepted for parity with the CLI, but has no effect in server mode - the response is always an `OperationOutcome`.

200.description: Validation completed. The `OperationOutcome` carries one issue per validation message; an outcome with no error-severity issues means the resource is valid.

400.description: A parameter was not recognised, or its value could not be parsed, or a `profile` could not be resolved (`Unable to resolve profile <url>`: load the IG that defines it first, with `/loadIG`).

post.description: Evaluates a FHIRPath expression against the posted resource. The result is returned as a `Parameters` resource with an `expression` parameter echoing the input and a `result` parameter holding the string form of the evaluation result.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.description: The FHIRPath expression to evaluate.

requestBody.description: The FHIR resource to evaluate the expression against.

200.description: Evaluation result as a `Parameters` resource. When the expression doesn't parse, or evaluating it fails, the response is still `200`, with an `OperationOutcome` that has an error saying why.

get.description: Static type checking of a FHIRPath expression, without evaluating it: the expression is parsed, then checked against the type it would be evaluated on. The result is an `OperationOutcome`, always with status `200` when the checking ran: an error issue when the expression doesn't parse (with its line and column) or doesn't check against the type (an unknown element, a function used on the wrong type, the wrong parameters...), a warning issue for each warning the checking raises (each with its message id), and, when there is no error, an information issue saying what type the expression returns. `POST` works the same way, with the same query parameters.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: The type the expression is evaluated on: a type name (a resource or data type), a path in a type, or the canonical URL of a StructureDefinition.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.description: The FHIRPath expression to check.

400.description: Missing `type` or `expression` parameter, or one that is too long (the type may be up to 1024 characters, the expression up to 10000).

post.description: As `GET /fhirpath/check`: the parameters are in the query; any body is ignored.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: The type the expression is evaluated on: a type name (a resource or data type), a path in a type, or the canonical URL of a StructureDefinition.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.description: The FHIRPath expression to check.

400.description: Missing `type` or `expression` parameter, or one that is too long (the type may be up to 1024 characters, the expression up to 10000).

post.summary: Compare a resource against a matchetype pattern
post.description: Compares an actual resource against an expected "matchetype" - a resource-shaped pattern whose values may be wildcards such as `$string$`, `$date$` or `$uuid$`. Both documents are supplied as JSON objects inside a single JSON wrapper; XML is not supported here.

matchetype.description: The expected pattern, optionally using wildcards.

200.description: Comparison result. An `OperationOutcome` with no error issues means the resource matches the pattern.

400.description: The body did not contain both `resource` and `matchetype`.

post.summary: Generate test data for a profile
post.description: Generates conformant example data for a profile. One resource is produced per row in `data`; with no `data` a single row of defaults is used. `mappings` bind row columns to element paths.

profile.description: Canonical URL of the StructureDefinition to generate against.

data.description: Rows of column name / value pairs. Defaults to one empty row.

mappings.description: Mappings from element path to a value expression.

bundle.description: The string `true` wraps all generated rows in a Bundle. Any other value, and absence, means one resource per row. Note this is compared as a string, so a JSON boolean `true` does not switch it on.

format.description: Output format for the generated resources.

200.description: The generated resource, or Bundle of resources.

400.description: Missing `profile` field, or the profile is not loaded (`Profile not found: <url>`).

post.summary: Load an implementation guide into the running engine
post.description: Loads an IG into the shared validation engine, making its profiles, value sets and maps available to every subsequent request. The value may be a package reference (`id#version`) or a URL. A path on the server's file system is accepted only while the server is bound to loopback (the default); with `-allowNetworkAccess` a path is refused with 400. The load is permanent for the lifetime of the process - there is no unload.

ig.description: Package reference or URL; a local path only while the server is bound to loopback.

400.description: Missing `ig` field, or a server-local path while the server is not bound to loopback.

post.summary: Convert a resource between JSON and XML
post.description: Re-serialises the posted resource. The input format comes from `Content-Type` and the output format from `Accept`; the FHIR version is unchanged.

post.summary: Convert a resource between FHIR versions
post.description: Converts the posted resource from the server's FHIR version to `targetVersion` using the native version convertors. Only resources that carry a `url` element can be converted - StructureMap-based conversion is not available in server mode, and anything else fails with a 500. The response uses the same format as the request.

parameters.name: targetVersion
parameters.description: Target FHIR version.

200.description: The resource in the target version.

post.summary: Generate the snapshot for a StructureDefinition
post.description: Takes a StructureDefinition carrying a differential and returns it with the snapshot generated. The base definition must be known to the engine. The response uses the same format as the request.

200.description: The StructureDefinition with its snapshot populated.

post.summary: Generate the narrative for a resource
post.description: Returns the posted resource with a generated human-readable narrative in `text.div`. The response uses the same format as the request.

200.description: The resource with its narrative populated.

post.summary: Apply a StructureMap to a resource
post.description: Runs the named StructureMap over the posted resource. The map, and any maps it depends on, must already be loaded (server start up `-ig`, or `/loadIG`). Input format comes from `Content-Type`, output format from `Accept`.

parameters.name: map
parameters.description: Canonical URL of the StructureMap to run.

get.summary: Fetch a StructureMap by canonical URL
get.description: Returns the StructureMap the engine holds for the given canonical URL, serialised in the format asked for by `Accept`. This handler does not check the HTTP method, so POST (and any other method) behave identically to GET.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Canonical URL of the StructureMap.

400.description: Missing `url` parameter, or the map is not loaded (`Unable to find map: <url>`).

500.description: The map could not be serialised.

post.summary: Start a run of the terminology ecosystem tests against a terminology server
post.description:
Starts a session for running the terminology ecosystem tests (`hl7.fhir.uv.tx-ecosystem`) one at a time with `GET /txTest`. The body holds the things that can't change during a run. The server is connected to now, and its FHIR version (from `$versions`, or `/metadata`) decides the FHIR version the tests are run in - it is not a setting. End the run with `POST /txTest/teardown`, which returns the reports, once the last test has returned. Sessions that are never torn down last for the life of the process.

Only available when the server was started with `-txTests` (a `404` otherwise). When the server is not bound to loopback, only servers configured in `fhir-settings.json` can be tested (a `403` otherwise).

server.description: Base URL of the terminology server under test.

test-version.description: Which published version of the test cases to run, e.g. `1.9.6` - a version of the tx-ecosystem IG, not a FHIR version. `current` is the ci-build, which changes whenever the tests do: pin a version in a pipeline.

externals.description: The content of an externals file (in the format of `tests/messages-tx.fhir.org.json`), which lets the server use its own wording for messages. The JSON itself, not a file name. Without it, messages are checked against the fragments in the expected responses.

folder.description: Names the run's output folder inside the validator's temporary directory - a simple name, not a path. Defaults to the server's host name.

tester.description: Who is running the tests, for `TestReport.tester` (default `HL7 Ecosystem Test Runner`). The modes are added after it.

test-version.description: The version of the test cases that was loaded.

fhirVersion.description: The server's FHIR version, which the tests run in.

software.description: The server's software and version, from its CapabilityStatement.

features.description: The features the server declares, which decide which suites and tests with a `feature` run.

output.description: The folder the run writes to.

400.description: The body is not a JSON object, a required parameter is missing, or a parameter is invalid.

403.description: The server is not bound to loopback, and the terminology server is not configured in fhir-settings.

404.description: The terminology test endpoints are not enabled (`-txTests`).

500.description: The test cases could not be loaded, or the server could not be connected to (or its FHIR version determined).

get.summary: Run one terminology ecosystem test case
get.description:
Runs one test in a session started with `POST /txTest/setup`. The test cases and the suite's setup resources are loaded once, and reused. A test that doesn't run - it is disabled, or gated on a mode that wasn't requested, a feature the server doesn't declare, or a FHIR version the server isn't - returns an error saying why, but is not counted in the run's results.

The older form, with `server` (and optionally `externals`, naming a file in the test package, and `folder`) in place of `session`, still works: it makes an implicit session for that server, with the `current` test cases, on its first call. That session can be ended with `POST /txTest/teardown?server=...`.

Only available when the server was started with `-txTests` (a `404` otherwise). When the server is not bound to loopback, only servers configured in `fhir-settings.json` can be tested (a `403` otherwise).

parameters.name: session
parameters.description: The session id from `POST /txTest/setup`.

parameters.name: suite
parameters.description: Name of the test suite.

parameters.name: test
parameters.description: Name of the test within the suite.

parameters.name: modes
parameters.description: Comma separated list of test modes. Pass every mode the server supports: a test gated on a mode that isn't passed doesn't run. Defaults to `general,snomed,omop,mimetypes,icd-11,icf,loinc` - everything except the tx.fhir.org specific tests.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: Names a subfolder of the run's output folder for this test's expected/actual files, so that a test run more than one way keeps each run's diffs. A simple name, not a path.

parameters.name: server
parameters.description: Legacy: the server under test, in place of `session`.

200.description: The call completed. An information-severity `OperationOutcome` means the test passed; an error-severity outcome carries the failure message, or why the test did not run.

400.description: A required parameter is missing or invalid, or a parameter that setup fixes was passed with a session.

403.description: Legacy form only: the server is not bound to loopback, and the terminology server is not configured in fhir-settings.

404.description: The session, suite or test is not known, or the terminology test endpoints are not enabled (`-txTests`).

post.summary: End a run, and get its reports
post.description:
Ends the session, and returns the two reports a command line run writes: `test-results.json` and `report.json` (a FHIR `TestReport`, with a score and an overall pass/fail). Both are also written to the run's output folder. Tests that did not run are not counted; a test run more than once counts once, with its last result. The session ends first: a later test call or teardown for it is a `404`, and a test still running at teardown is not in the reports.

Only available when the server was started with `-txTests` (a `404` otherwise).

parameters.name: session
parameters.description: The session id from `POST /txTest/setup`.

parameters.name: server
parameters.description: Legacy: ends the implicit session for this server.

output.description: The folder the reports were written to.

test-results.description: test-results.json: the date of the run, and every suite and test that ran, with its status and, for failures, the message.

report.description: report.json: the run as a FHIR TestReport.

404.description: The session is not known (or has already been torn down), or the terminology test endpoints are not enabled (`-txTests`).

500.description: The reports could not be written.

post.description: Responds, then stops the HTTP server and exits the JVM about 100ms later. POST only - a GET returns 405.

200.description: Shutdown accepted; the process exits shortly afterwards.

get.description: Serves this specification as JSON, with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` so that the documentation pages can load it.
HTML page that renders `/openapi.json` with Swagger UI. The Swagger assets are loaded from unpkg.com, so this page needs internet access in the browser.
HTML page that renders `/openapi.json` with Redoc. The Redoc bundle is loaded from cdn.redoc.ly, so this page needs internet access in the browser.

BadRequest.description: A parameter was not recognised, or its value could not be parsed.

MethodNotAllowed.description: The HTTP method is not supported by this endpoint.

ServerError.description: The operation failed. The outcome carries the failure message.

OperationOutcome.description: FHIR OperationOutcome resource carrying validation messages or error details. Only the elements the service populates are described here.
